assessments.affected_condition: Caller passes a non-NULL X509_INFO stack into PEM_X509_INFO_read[_bio][_ex] and reuses/frees it after read failure.
assessments.assessment: No calls to that family in the pinned Node crypto bindings/ncrypto, .NET OpenSSL shim or libpq TLS consumer. Node CA/file loading uses PEM_read_bio_X509 or PEM_read_bio_X509_AUX with null object arguments; .NET uses those same individual certificate APIs. libpq delegates root store loading through SSL_CTX_load_verify_locations/default paths. OpenSSL advisory states its own TLS CA-loading callers always pass NULL.
limits: Underlying affected OpenSSL code remains present. This is a caller exclusion, not a vendor-unaffected claim.
Other native consumers such as API curl require their own assessment.
reassess_if: Runtime/native dependency or crypto source changes
CMS/PKCS7 encryption or verification, user-supplied certificate/CRL stores or DANE is introduced

assessments.affected_condition: CMS_encrypt/CMS_encrypt_ex encrypt to an attacker-controlled EC certificate with group order 1.
assessments.assessment: No CMS_encrypt[_ex] call or binding in reviewed Node crypto/ncrypto, .NET crypto shim or libpq TLS consumer. .NET AnyOS uses ManagedPkcsPal, constructs EnvelopedData in managed code and encrypts recipient keys through managed RSA APIs. Ordinary TLS/QUIC does not use affected CMS_encrypt path per advisory. Production application search found no CMS consumption/encryption feature.
limits: No CMS library-wide safety claim. New native CMS callers or arbitrary EC certificate workflows require reassessment.

assessments.affected_condition: DANE-enabled TLS client combines PKIX-TA/PKIX-EE and DANE-TA TLSA validation through OpenSSL DANE APIs.
assessments.assessment: Pinned Node crypto/ncrypto and .NET shim expose no OpenSSL DANE initialization/TLSA APIs; libpq TLS source also has no DANE operation. Supported application configuration contains no DANE client or custom native binding. Actual .NET/libpq binaries contain no strings for the named DANE imports, while ordinary X509 store/check symbols are present.
limits: Ordinary TLS use is not proof of DANE use. DANE may be available in underlying OpenSSL; no removal claim.
Does not cover curl/DANE-capable external tools or new custom native networking clients.

assessments.scope: Pinned Node 24.22.3, .NET 10.0.15 crypto PAL and libpq 19.0-2.pgdg13+1 used by supported RateFreak application/maintenance flows. Not a clearance of all native consumers, API curl, separate services or host.
assessments.affected_condition: OpenSSL CMS_verify/PKCS7_verify with CRL checking enabled accepts hostile SignedData containing both CRL distribution points and candidate CRLs, causing repeated relative-name rebuilding.
assessments.assessment: No CMS_verify/PKCS7_verify operation in reviewed Node bindings/ncrypto, .NET shim or libpq. .NET SignedCms delegates signature checking to managed SignerInfo; SignerInfo verifies the cryptographic signature before X509Chain.Build, and does not import SignedData CRLs into a native CMS verification store. Its online revocation support is present and must not be described as absent. Node and libpq can enable CRL checking using application/operator-supplied CRLs, but the supported RateFreak application does not provide a hostile CMS-to-CRL verification endpoint.
limits: The advisory also notes TLS uses local CRLs, so this does not assert that every CRL-enabled TLS configuration has zero CPU cost.
New CMS verification, untrusted CRL-store provisioning, revocation configuration or native crypto callers require reassessment.
reassess_if: Runtime/native dependency or crypto source changes
CMS/PKCS7 encryption or verification, user-supplied certificate/CRL stores or DANE is introduced

scope_limit: Four advisory conditions, three reviewed consumer families; not overall release/security clearance. No exploit harness or complete dynamic callgraph proof performed.
